traits.stem_form.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-19), Lophophora: Lophophora: stems usually gray-green or blue-green to dark green, usually flat-topped and cryptic in the soil surface, sometimes protruding above it with a recessed apex, ribbed or weakly tuberculate, 2-7.5 × (4-)5-12 cm, softly fleshy, dull, glabrous; ribs 5, 8 or 13 (rarely 21), low, broadly rounded, straight; areoles 3-15+ mm apart along the ribs or at the apices of low, humplike tubercles, copiously hairy, the hairs in compact erect tufts to 7-10 mm. Spines absent. Flowers deeply nestled in the areolar hairs at the stem apex, campanulate, 1-3 × (1-)1.5-2.5 cm; ovary smooth, scales, hairs and spines absent. Fruits white to pinkish, clavate to nearly cylindric, 11-25 × (2-)4-5 mm, spines and scales absent. The top depressed from its 'recessed apex' (and the species' 'deeply depressed centre').
